sentences.text: L.Appalanaidu vs K.Sitaram Amp Anr on 8 May, 2024
In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh

At Amaravati [3364]
 Wednesday, The Eighth Day Of May Two Thousand And
 Twenty Four
 Present
 The Honourable Sri Justice A V Ravindra Babu
Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No: 1718/2016
Between:
 1. L. Appalanaidu, S/O Late Sanyasi @ Sanyasappadu,
 Labourer, R/O Bhupalapuram Vilalge, Gurla Mandal,
 Vizianagaram District.
 ...Appellant

And
 1. K. Sitaram, S/O Pyditalli, Owner Of Auto No.Ap.35-T-
 5661, R/O Sc Street, Kella Village, Gurla Mandal,
 Vizianagaram District.

2. United India Insurance Company Limited, Rep. By Its
 Divisional Manager O/O Visakhapatnam.

...Respondents
The Court made the following:
Judgment:

-
Challenge in this MACMA is to the award, dated 20.04.2009 in Original Petition No.423 of 2007, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge,
Vizianagaram ("Tribunal" for short), whereunder the Tribunal dealing with a claim for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- made by the petitioner on account of injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident, which was occurred on 24.02.2007, awarded a sum of Rs.67,250/-.
2) The parties to this MACMA will hereinafter be referred to as described before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
L.Appalanaidu vs K.Sitaram Amp Anr on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75730658/
1 3)
The petitioner laid a claim before the tribunal for "no fault liability" under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that on 24.02.2007 the petitioner boarded the auto bearing No.A.P.35-T-5661 (hereinafter will be referred to as "offending vehicle") to go to his village along with some other passengers.
When the auto reached near Chukkapeta junction at about 4-00 p.m., the driver drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and applied sudden brakes when a bullock cart came across the road.
Consequently, the auto turned turtle and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his left leg.

Immediately, he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Vizianagaram.
The doctors took X-rays and found fracture to his left leg.
After discharge from the Government Hospital, the petitioner was admitted in Sai Vamsi Nursing Home, Vizianagaram.
The doctors conducted surgery and inserted implants in his left leg.
The petitioner suffered lot of pain.
The doctors suggested the petitioner to take bed rest for a period of two months.
The petitioner was working as labourer and earning Rs.3,000/- per month prior to the accident.
The police of Gurla registered a case in Cr.No.14/2007 under Sections 337 and 338 of the Indian Penal Code against the auto driver.
The first respondent is owner of the offending vehicle whereas the second respondent is its insurer.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4) The first respondent remained exparte.

5) The second respondent got filed a counter putting burden on the petitioner to prove the manner of accident, age and income of the petitioner and the insurance coverage to the auto and contending in substance that the auto driver had no valid driving license as on the date of accident.
The first respondent being the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle knows well that he has no valid and subsisting driving license at the time of accident.
Hence, their company has no liability to pay any compensation.
The claim of the petitioner is highly excessive.
Therefore, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6) On the basis of the above pleadings, the tribunal settled the following issues for trail:
(1) Whether the pleaded accident was occurred resulting in injuries to the petitioner,
due to his involvement in a motor vehicle accident involving the auto bearing No.A.P.35-T-5661 when it was used in a public place?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation and, if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of the respondents?
(3) To what relief?
7)
During the course of enquiry, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and examined P.W.2, the doctor, who issued disability certificate and got marked Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.9.
Further Ex.X.1 to Ex.X.4 were marked.
On behalf of the second respondent, R.W.1 and R.W.2 were examined and Ex.B.1 and Ex.B.2 were marked.

8) The tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral as well as documentary evidence held that the accident occurred was due to involvement of L.Appalanaidu vs K.Sitaram Amp Anr on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75730658/
2 offending vehicle and further awarded a sum of Rs.67,250/- towards compensation.
The petitioner felt aggrieved that the compensation so awarded is not just and reasonable, filed the present MACMA.

9) Now, in deciding the present MACMA, the point for determination is whether the award, dated 20.04.2009 in Original Petition No.423 of 2007, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge,
Vizianagaram, in awarding compensation of Rs.67,250/- as against the original claim of Rs.1,50,000/-, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to enhance the compensation?
POINT:-
10)

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District Judge,
Vizianagaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Sri M.S. Bhanu Prasad Rao, learned counsel, representing Sri Abburi Jitendra,
learned counsel for the appellant, would contend that the tribunal as against the original claim of Rs.1,50,000/-, awarded compensation of Rs.67,250/- and the difference amount is Rs.82,750/-.
The tribunal did not compute the compensation properly.
The tribunal ought to have awarded more compensation considering the disability, as such, MACMA is liable to be allowed.

11) M/s.P. Satya Manjula, learned counsel for the second respondent through video conference,
would canvass the contention that the claim was laid under Section 163-A of M.V. Act, 1988 and the tribunal considered the compensation as Rs.2,000/- insofar as the injuries sustained by the petitioner and further awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- for the grievous injury looking into Schedule-II of Section 163-A of M.V. Act.
The tribunal considered the disability of 25%.
The injured could not prove that the income of him was Rs.30,000/- per annum.

The tribunal rightly considered the income of the injured as Rs.15,000/- per annum and applied proper multiplier according to Schedule as '15' and arrived at the loss of earnings Rs.56,250/- towards 25% disability.
The tribunal awarded Rs.2,000/- for medical expenditure because the petitioner did not file any proof regarding medical expenditure properly.
The learned counsel would contend that MACMA is liable to be dismissed.

12) As seen from the evidence of P.W.1, he put forth the facts in tune with the pleadings and through his examination Ex.A.1 to Ex.A.9 were marked.
13)
The petitioner examined P.W.2, the medical officer, who treated him.

It is to be noted that though claim was laid under Section 163-A of M.V. Act, but it was filed with the allegations that the accident occurred was due to rash and negligent driving made by the driver of the offending vehicle who applied sudden brakes when a bullock cart came across the road.
The tribunal held that there is no need to prove the rash and negligent act.

So, the tribunal considered the evidence of P.W.1,
Ex.A.1 copy of FIR and Ex.A.4 copy of charge sheet and made appropriate finding that there was involvement of the offending vehicle in the episode, as such, the petitioner received injuries.
Therefore, finding of facts cannot be disturbed.
L.Appalanaidu vs K.Sitaram Amp Anr on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75730658/
3 14)
As seen from Ex.A.2 wound certificate, there was deformity of middle of left thigh, laceration 1 x 1.2 cm x muscle deep, fresh and bleeding and two abrasions near right knee.
The tribunal considered the evidence of P.W.2 that he assessed the disability of the petitioner at 25% which is partial and permanent in nature.
The tribunal took into consideration Ex.A7, disability certificate.

As there was no evidence to prove that the petitioner was earning Rs.3,000/- per month by doing labour work prior to accident, the tribunal applied notional theory and arrived at the income as that of Rs.15,000/- per annum as per Schedule- II of Section 163-A of M.V. Act.
The period of accident was in the year 2007.
Hence, the notional income of Rs.15,000/- per annum arrived at by the tribunal cannot be found fault.

If the amount of Rs.15,000/- per annum arrived at by the tribunal is reasonable, there is no dispute about the compute of compensation as Rs.15,000/- x 15 x 25% which comes to Rs.56,250/- towards 25% disability.

The tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,000/- +
Rs.5,000/- towards simple and grievous injuries and further awarded Rs.2,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Though the petitioner did not prove the medical expenditure properly, the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,000/- towards medical expenditure.

Therefore, the overall compensation arrived at by the tribunal is Rs.67,250/- under Section 163- A of M.V. Act, 1988 appears to be reasonable, as such, there are no grounds to interfere with the same.
15) In the result, the MACMA is dismissed, but under the circumstances, without costs.
The second respondent shall deposit the rest of compensation, if any, within a period of one month from this day.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.08.05.2024.
